en: The Mañjuvajra-stotra composed by Mañjugarbha. Homage to the glorious Mañjuvajra!
Resplendent like the moon, holding a sword and a book in his hands, most beautiful and tranquil, a youth wearing five locks of hair,
possessing the most excellent and vast liberation, with eyes as broad as lotus petals.
I pay homage to Mañjughoṣa, who is skilled in burning away evil intellect. || 1 ||
He who has mounted the vehicle of the enemy of beasts (the lion), who has bestowed the gift of food, who is the vehicle for gods, asuras, and men, who is preeminent among Bodhisattvas,
who is a treasury of all virtues, and who is the canopy of all branches of knowledge.
I bow to Mañjughoṣa, whose arrow is the lotus of his hand. || 2 ||
[To him] who has distributed all his treasures, who has washed away the stain of ignorance, who is pleased by remembrance and worship, who is free from the defects of passion and the like,
who provides nourishment for the gods, and who is the consort of the one called the Giver of Siddhis—
I bow to Mañjughoṣa, who has completely dried up the dullness produced by [ignorance]. || 3 ||
Surrounded by Gaṇapati, Śarajanman, Śrī Mahākāla, and Siṃha, he has the luster of the moon, lotus-like eyes,
and bears a sword, an arrow, a rosary, and a book.
I bow to Mañjughoṣa, who wears a lovely garland upon his chest. || 4 ||
This one, whose face is smiling and who is surrounded by the guardians of Mitra, Agni, Rakṣas, Pavana, and Pramatha— even for the sake of subduing the Lord of the Gods—
has the body of the king of birds (Garuḍa) and is worthy of worship by Brahmā; [he is] Rama-Umā...
I bow to Mañjughoṣa, who is devoted to the performance of what has been prescribed. || 5 ||
Where the path was traversed by the cutting edge of his sword, and where every stream of water fell upon his limbs as he chanted mantras,
even now that river on the ground shines forth at the site of his many practices.
I bow to Mañjughoṣa, who possesses exceedingly great majesty. || 6 ||
Pleased by your fresh hymn of praise, the Goddess of the Secret,
who is the essence of all the Vedas and is supremely radiant, shone forth;
she is the further shore of the ocean of worldly existence and the pinnacle of the wish-fulfilling tree of charity.
I bow to Mañjughoṣa, who has caused the great pride of the Māras to fall away. || 7 ||
The world of beings distinguishes the realm of phenomena as the Great Lord,
situated upon a thousand-petaled lotus as the light of sovereignty;
yet even that is Your own praiseworthy divine majesty, O Lord.
I bow to Mañjughoṣa, who analyzes the lord of serpents. || 8 ||
He who recites this desired *mālinī* verse composition becomes a king among poets, seated upon the lion-throne of debate,
with the nectar of his speech shining brilliantly in all assemblies.
Having mastered all branches of knowledge, he was adorned with excellence and possessed skill in what is beneficial.
The Mañjuvajra-stotra, extracted from the Svayambhū-purāṇa and composed by Mañjugarbha, is completed.
